finding.claim: With acceptOversizedBlocks enabled, compressedLen from an untrusted 21-byte block header is unbounded (only < 0 is rejected), so the decoder allocates up to ~2 GB before any read, causing OOM. Opt-in only; default config is bounded by originalLen.
finding.source: Block header bytes from untrusted stream read at LZ4BlockInputStream.java:279 (compressedLen)
finding.sink: LZ4BlockInputStream.java:311-312 compressedBuffer = new byte[Math.max(compressedLen, ...)] before readFully at line 314

trace.note: compressedLen read from header with no upper bound
compressedLen < originalLen check skipped when acceptOversizedBlocks is true
allocation of Math.max(compressedLen, buf*3/2) bytes happens before any read
readFully only detects truncation after allocation
withAcceptOversizedBlocks(true) builder option enables the unbounded path

finding.guards_checked: compressedLen < 0 (line 285) is the only bound. Default acceptOversizedBlocks=false bounds compressedLen < originalLen (line 289), so the default path is safe. The EOF check in readFully runs after the allocation and does not limit it. Safe paths checked and not reported: deprecated constructors use the non-insecure fast decoder (LZ4Factory.java:98,243-247); generated decompressors check matchOff < destOff (decompress.template:113) and bounds; JNI entry points call checkRange before native code; LZ4FrameInputStream bounds blockSize by a 4 MB BD max and verifies checksums before decompression.
